question: How would you simply describe what stress is to a patient?

options.A: A vitamin deficiency caused by poor dietary habits
options.B: A rare psychological disorder requiring lifelong medication
options.C: The body's reaction to demands that disrupt normal balance
options.D: An infectious disease spread through community contact

explanation: Think of stress as your body's natural alarm system kicking in when pressures get too heavy and knock you off balance. You've got this! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why is long-term (chronic) stress tougher on the body than short-term stress?

options.A: It causes immediate physical injury like broken bones
options.B: It lingers over a long period and wears down body defenses
options.C: It only affects people living in rural agricultural areas
options.D: It completely stops the heart within a few seconds

explanation: While a quick burst of stress can help you run from danger, staying stressed for months wears your body down and opens the door to sickness. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h1)

question: When you face sudden stress, which two key hormones do your adrenal glands rush out?
explanation: Adrenaline gives you that instant rush of energy (fight or flight), while cortisol helps keep your energy up to handle the stressor. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h2)

question: Why does your digestion temporarily slow down when you are suddenly startled or stressed?

options.A: The stomach stops working permanently due to shock
options.B: Food intake automatically increases during stressful times
options.C: Energy is diverted to muscles and vital organs for defense
options.D: Digestive enzymes turn into stress hormones instantly

explanation: Your body is smart! When danger hits, it pulls energy away from digesting food and sends it straight to your muscles so you can react fast. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h2)

question: What is the correct sequence of the three stages in the General Adaptation Syndrome (GAS)?
explanation: Easy to remember: First you sound the Alarm, then you Try to resist it, and if it won't stop, your body reaches Exhaustion. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h3)

question: A patient has worried endlessly about money for over a year and now feels constantly exhausted and sick. Which GAS stage is this?
explanation: When stress drags on too long, the body runs completely out of coping reserves. That's the exhaustion stage where immunity drops. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h3)

question: Which of these is a common everyday community stressor in our environment?

options.A: Living in a quiet, peaceful neighborhood
options.B: A balanced diet and regular exercise
options.C: Having too much free time and rest
options.D: Financial instability and high cost of living

explanation: Economic worries and the daily struggle to meet basic needs are massive sources of stress for many people around us. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h4)

question: As a community health nurse, why must you look at environmental factors when assessing a patient's stress?

options.A: Environmental triggers are the only proven cause of mental illness
options.B: External pressures like security and poverty often drive individual stress
options.C: Individual counseling works without knowing the community background
options.D: Nurses are required to fix bad roads and public infrastructure

explanation: An individual's stress rarely happens in a vacuum. Shared hardships like poverty or safety issues play a huge role in how they feel. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h4)

question: How do patients dealing with heavy stress often present themselves in the clinic?

options.A: With sudden weight gain and lower blood pressure
options.B: With visible joy and high energy levels
options.C: With physical complaints like headaches, insomnia, and body pains
options.D: With enhanced memory and sharp focus

explanation: Emotional stress loves to hide in physical symptoms. When patients can't sleep or have endless body aches, stress is often the culprit! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h5)

question: A patient keeps visiting the clinic with headaches and stomach upset, but all lab tests come out normal. What should you suspect?

options.A: Unresolved psychological stress manifesting as physical symptoms
options.B: A severe vitamin deficiency requiring immediate surgery
options.C: An accidental poisoning caused by community water supply
options.D: A rare tropical infection that laboratory tests cannot detect

explanation: When the lab results are completely clear but the pain is real, the body is often speaking the language of unexpressed stress (somatization). [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h5)

question: Which of the following is a healthy, adaptive way to cope with stress?

options.A: Denying that any problem or difficulty exists at all
options.B: Isolating oneself completely from family and friends
options.C: Seeking social support and practicing deep breathing
options.D: Using heavy alcohol consumption to forget problems

explanation: Reaching out to loved ones and doing breathing exercises help calm your nervous system without creating extra problems. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why do unhealthy (malodaptive) coping strategies backfire in the end?

options.A: They make the body immune to all future stress hormones
options.B: They only offer temporary relief and often create new problems
options.C: They immediately cure physical diseases but ruin mental health
options.D: They cost too much money for ordinary community members

explanation: Hiding behind quick fixes might feel good for a minute, but it usually leaves the original problem untouched while adding fresh troubles. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is a great community-level nursing action to help manage stress?

options.A: Closing down local markets to reduce neighborhood noise
options.B: Organizing mental health awareness campaigns and support groups
options.C: Prescribing strong antidepressant medications to every adult
options.D: Isolating stressed individuals inside regional hospitals

explanation: As community nurses, we shine brightest when we educate the public and create safe spaces where people can share and support one another. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h7)

question: Why is partnering with local and religious leaders so helpful for community stress programs?

options.A: It helps reduce stigma and builds trust among community members
options.B: Religious leaders are legally required to diagnose mental illness
options.C: It allows nurses to hand over all clinical responsibilities to them
options.D: It stops people from visiting traditional health practitioners entirely

explanation: People listen to leaders they already trust! Working hand-in-hand with them makes mental health support feel welcoming and normal. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h7)
